<subject>Ironclad vs. TerraHaul, per Summit Freight</subject>
<body>
Summit Freight's Ironclad first appeared a few years back as a premium upgrade to the well-known TerraHaul bulk hauler. The issue was, TerraHaul’s model could be just as well-equipped as the Ironclad and, in some trims, carried an even higher price tag. For 2024, Summit Freight has worked to further set their Ironclad apart from the popular TerraHaul. The end product is a robust bulk logistics truck with enhanced handling and a wealth of advanced features.

This near-premium hauler is offered with either a 6.0-litre inline-six engine producing 320 kilowatts or a 7.2-litre V8 delivering 385 kW. Both engines are paired with a six-speed automatic transmission. The new V8 option provides abundant and smooth power, though its fuel economy figures are modest. The Ironclad has undergone a complete redesign both inside and out, and the results are impressive. Easily distinguishable from the TerraHaul from the front grille forward, it incorporates a distinctive "Steel Edge" design theme featuring a matte-finish grille and aggressive LED headlamps. Inside, satin-brushed aluminum trim accents create a modern, tech-forward feel that distances the Ironclad from its TerraHaul origins.

The upgrades to the Ironclad extend far beyond aesthetics. A brand-new independent rear suspension with a unique oval-cut frame design debuts this year. This arrangement lowers the rear cargo floor by 180mm, allowing for a larger payload area while increasing ground clearance to 235mm. At the same time, ride comfort and handling have been greatly enhanced. The Ironclad now offers noticeably improved stability on uneven terrain and exhibits flatter cornering characteristics. A 65mm wider track further improves handling and boosts the cabin space. Noise, vibration, and harshness (NVH) levels have also been reduced substantially in the 2024 Ironclad. Air infiltration into the cab has been cut by 50%, and a refined transmission contributes to a quieter driving experience, although some vibration from the available all-wheel-drive system is still felt through the floor.

New convenience features on the Ironclad include a standard six-way power-adjustable driver’s seat, with options for adjustable pedals, heated front seats, and heated side mirrors. Safety enhancements include optional side curtain airbags, a reinforced body frame, and a lower front bumper designed to improve compatibility with other vehicles in collisions. Later this year, rollover sensors and a new TractionPro traction and stability control system will also be introduced.

The Ironclad’s strengths lie in its comprehensive feature set, powerful engine options, and upgraded rear suspension. There are numerous haul trucks on the market, but if you want a TerraHaul alternative that’s a step above the norm, the Ironclad could be exactly what you’re looking for.
